headline: Sheikh Hasina and 33 others indicted in truck driver killing case
summary: A special court in Dhaka has framed charges against the deposed prime minister and several former ministers for the death of 25-year-old Mohammad Hossain.
details: A special court in Dhaka has framed charges against the deposed prime minister Sheikh Hasina and 33 others. The case is linked to the killing of a truck driver during the July uprising.
Judge Md Rabiul Alam of the Special Judge’s Court-4 passed the order, according to court bench assistant Belal Hossain.
The victim, 25-year-old Mohammad Hossain, was killed in Dhaka’s Mohammadpur area during protests on July 19, 2024.
The case was initiated after his mother, Rina Begum, filed a murder case with the court on August 27, accusing Hasina and 15 others.
Eleven accused, including former ICT state minister Zunaid Ahmed Palak and former lawmaker Sadek Khan, pleaded not guilty.
Arrest warrants have been issued against 23 absconding accused, including Sheikh Hasina and former ministers Obaidul Quader, Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal, Mohammed Hasan Mahmud, and Jahangir Kabir Nanak.
The court has fixed November 25 for recording the statements of prosecution witnesses.
According to court records and police, 920 cases, including 560 linked to killings, have been filed with various police stations in Dhaka till July this year.

headline: CPB activists attacked in Paltan over 'Joy Bangla' slogans
summary: The Communist Party of Bangladesh (CPB) alleges a mob attack on its members during a solidarity rally in Dhaka, claiming the assault was triggered by slogans used during the march.
details: The Communist Party of Bangladesh (CPB) has alleged that its activists were attacked by a mob in front of the party's central office in Paltan, Dhaka, on Monday night.

The incident occurred during a solidarity rally organized by student and youth union activists to welcome back Deepak Sheel, the former president of the Student Union, who had been detained by police earlier that day.
According to CPB General Secretary Abdullah Al Kafi, the attack was carried out by a mob under the pretext of activists shouting 'Joy Bangla' slogans during the procession.
The party alleges that the mob was formed by activists from the former ruling party, though local BNP leaders have denied these allegations.
During the clash, Iran Molla, President of the Dhaka Metropolitan North Youth Union, and General Secretary Sohel Fakir were reportedly seized by the mob and handed over to the police.
Both leaders were released by the police at midnight. CPB leadership has strongly condemned the attack and demanded immediate action against those involved in the harassment and violence.
caption:
A mob attack in Paltan targets CPB activists over 'Joy Bangla' slogans. Two leaders were seized and handed over to the police.

The Communist Party of Bangladesh (CPB) has alleged that its activists were attacked by a mob in front of the party's central office in Paltan, Dhaka, on Monday night.

The incident occurred during a solidarity rally organized by student and youth union activists to welcome back Deepak Sheel, the former president of the Student Union, who had been detained by police earlier that day.

According to CPB General Secretary Abdullah Al Kafi, the attack was carried out by a mob under the pretext of activists shouting 'Joy Bangla' slogans during the procession.

The party alleges that the mob was formed by activists from the former ruling party, though local BNP leaders have denied these allegations.

During the clash, Iran Molla, President of the Dhaka Metropolitan North Youth Union, and General Secretary Sohel Fakir were reportedly seized by the mob and handed over to the police.

Both leaders were released by the police at midnight. CPB leadership has strongly condemned the attack and demanded immediate action against those involved in the harassment and violence.
